title: NFTStakerPriceScaled priceScale magnitude unchecked — silent emission/runway mis-sizing
description: NFTStakerPriceScaled's immutable priceScale is unbounded and decimal-unchecked. The constructor only guards _priceScale != 0 (L230); there is no upper bound and no decimal-consistency check tying priceScale to the actual reward/price decimal regime. _recomputeSchedule multiplies latestPrice * priceScale (L435), so a wrong-magnitude deploy value silently mis-sizes the emission rate/runway. The contract structurally cannot verify priceScale == 10**(rewardDecimals - priceDecimals).
impact: No asset/principal/third-party impact. priceScale never touches the budget ledger; every payout is bounded by the real funded balance via _safePay's shortfall-revert. The only effect is mis-sizing the emission RATE/runway: too-high collapses runway (budget/R) so earliest stakers over-earn until premature depletion and emissions pause until a top-up; too-low floor-divides newRate toward zero, silently re-introducing the floor-to-zero degradation the contract exists to fix. Solvency-safe and owner-correctable via setTargetAPY (priceScale and targetAPY are independent linear factors on the rate).
attackPath: No attacker. Trigger is a deploy-time owner choice of the immutable priceScale.
1. Owner deploys NFTStakerPriceScaled with priceScale != 10**(rewardDecimals - priceDecimals).
2. Constructor only checks _priceScale != 0 (L230); no upper bound, no decimal-consistency check.
3. _recomputeSchedule multiplies latestPrice * priceScale (L435), silently mis-sizing the rate.

4. Effect manifests over time as collapsed runway / premature depletion (too-high) or floor-to-zero emission (too-low). No revert until an absurd overflow-scale (the obvious-misconfig leg, out of scope).
recommendation: Add a deploy-time invariant tying priceScale to the actual decimal regime, e.g. require(priceScale == 10 ** (rewardToken.decimals() - priceTokenDecimals)) in the constructor, or pass priceTokenDecimals and derive priceScale internally so the magnitude cannot be supplied inconsistently. At minimum, document the exact expected magnitude per dispatcher price-token decimal regime and bound priceScale to prevent silent over-sizing.
category: QA/Low operational footgun (Law-3 non-obvious deploy-time configuration hazard)
